subtitulo: Hedging a complaint about a backlog
descripcion: At C2 hedging is deployed with full awareness of its social cost: knowing that stacking hedges past a certain point stops sounding careful and starts sounding evasive, and choosing a single, well-placed hedge over three weak ones because it reads as more confident, not less.

cuadroReferencia.titulo: One strong hedge beats three weak ones
filas: I think it might possibly be a bit off
reads as evasive, undermines the claim
one hedge, reads as confident and precise
no hedge, used when the writer is actually sure

ejemplos.texto: I suspect this figure is off, and here's why.
This is wrong. I'm sure enough to say so plainly.
I could be wrong about this, but I doubt it.

notas: A single, precise hedge (I suspect) reads as more confident than three stacked ones, because it signals the speaker has already done the calibration.
Choosing not to hedge at all, when genuinely certain, is itself a marked and effective choice at this level.
I could be wrong about this, but I doubt it is a controlled way to hedge and then immediately withdraw most of the hedge.

es.en: Spanish often doubles hedges («creo que quizás…»), and the habit transfers into English as stacked hedges (I think maybe it might…). English at this level rewards one precisely chosen hedge; stacking reads as uncertain rather than careful.
es.es: El español duplica a menudo los atenuantes («creo que quizás…»), y ese hábito pasa al inglés como acumulación («I think maybe it might…»). A este nivel, el inglés premia un solo «hedge» elegido con precisión; acumularlos suena inseguro, no cuidadoso.

de.en: German hedges with particles and adverbs («vielleicht», «eventuell», «wohl»), and stacking them produces perhaps possibly it might…. «Eventuell» is also a false friend: it means possibly, not eventually.
de.de: Deutsch schwächt mit Partikeln und Adverbien ab («vielleicht, eventuell, wohl»), und beim Stapeln entsteht leicht «perhaps possibly it might…». «Eventuell» ist außerdem ein falscher Freund: Es bedeutet «possibly», nicht «eventually».

it.en: Italian combines the «condizionale» with «forse» («forse potrebbe…»), which transfers as perhaps it might…. English at this level prefers a single, precisely chosen hedge.
it.it: L'italiano combina il condizionale con «forse» («forse potrebbe…»), che si trasferisce come «perhaps it might…». A questo livello l'inglese preferisce un solo «hedge» scelto con precisione.

fr.en: French often combines «peut-être» with the «conditionnel» («peut-être que cela pourrait…»), which transfers as perhaps it could…. English at this level prefers a single, precisely chosen hedge.
fr.fr: Le français combine souvent «peut-être» avec le conditionnel («peut-être que cela pourrait…»), ce qui se transfère en «perhaps it could…». À ce niveau, l'anglais préfère un seul «hedge» choisi avec précision.

pt.en: Portuguese combines «talvez» with the subjunctive or a modal («talvez possa…»), which transfers as perhaps it may…. English at this level prefers a single, precisely chosen hedge.
pt.pt: O português combina «talvez» com o subjuntivo ou com um modal («talvez possa…»), o que se transfere como «perhaps it may…». Nesse nível, o inglês prefere um único «hedge» escolhido com precisão.

errores: Stacking multiple hedges on a single claim, which reads as evasive rather than careful.
Hedging a claim the writer is actually certain about, undermining their own authority.
Using a hedge without any reasoning behind it, so it reads as reflexive rather than calibrated.

es: «*Por así decirlo*» rendered as *For so to say it* instead of *So to speak*.
de: «*sozusagen*» rendered as *so to say* instead of *so to speak*.
it: «*Per così dire*» rendered as *For so to say* instead of *So to speak*.
fr: «*Pour ainsi dire*» rendered as *For so to say* instead of *So to speak*.
pt: «*Por assim dizer*» rendered as *For so to say* instead of *So to speak*.

mision.consigna: Write to an authority about a case that has been stuck for months, hedged exactly as far as your evidence goes.
requisitos: no more than two hedges in the whole text
one claim stated flat, and a line saying why
one *As far as I can tell*
use *a backlog*, *to chase something up* and *to lodge an appeal*

microtareas.texto: Write three claims about the delay. Hedge each only as far as you can support it.
Remove one hedge that makes you sound weaker than your evidence.
Record 2 minutes on being *passed from pillar to post*. Careful, not evasive.

autochequeo: Is any claim hedged more than once, stacking weakens it?
Is a claim the writer is actually certain about left unhedged?
Does each hedge carry a reason, not just reflexive caution?
Would the writing read as confident overall, not evasive?
Is there at least one deliberately unhedged claim for contrast?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on hedging density. Flag any claim with more than one stacked hedge, and flag any certain claim left unnecessarily hedged. Do not rewrite the text.
